Where it began

He was born in Sialkot on 24 April 1986 and studied at the Pakistan Air Force College in Lower Topa, hoping to become a pilot. In 2002 his family moved to Zimbabwe. He went on to Scotland to read software engineering at Glasgow Caledonian University, and it was in Scottish club cricket that he found out how good he could be, hitting three Twenty20 hundreds for Weirs in a single season.

He made his first-class debut in Zimbabwe in 2007, became a Zimbabwean citizen in 2011 and played his first international in 2013.

The player

He batted right-handed and bowled off-spin, and Zimbabwe used him for both. His Test debut came against Pakistan in Harare on 3 September 2013, and he made 60. Over 22 Tests, up to 2025, he scored 1,434 runs at 34.14, with one hundred and 11 fifties, and took 40 wickets, including two five-wicket hauls.

His hundred came against Sri Lanka in 2017, on the tour when Zimbabwe also won an ODI series there for the first time. Against West Indies he passed 80 in both innings and took five wickets in the same Test, a mix only Jacques Kallis had managed before, and Zimbabwe held on for a draw. In 2020 he took 7 for 113 against Sri Lanka, among the best figures by a Zimbabwe bowler in Tests.

What made him special

He gives his side everything. He bowled 43 overs in that innings against Sri Lanka, and he will bat wherever the team needs him. In one-day cricket he has made run chases his speciality, with three hundreds in chases in a single month in 2022.

If one thing has eluded him in Tests, it is the second hundred, which has kept him waiting through 11 fifties. Fair to say he made up for it elsewhere.

Away from the middle

He captains Zimbabwe in Twenty20 cricket, and in 2024 he became the first Zimbabwean to make a T20 international hundred, 133 not out from 43 balls. In 2026 he led his side into the Super 8 stage of the T20 World Cup, beating Australia on the way. He has played in leagues all over the world, and in 2023 he became the first Zimbabwean to hit a fifty in the IPL.

And finally

Here is a curious one for the record books. In 42 Test innings, he was never once not out. Every single time, the bowlers had to come and get him.
